title: Iquique march seeking government response to crime and insecurity
location: Plaza Prat and central avenues, Iquique
participants_original: La Tercera body attributes 500–600 to Carabineros; embedded police X post says around 450 at one route point/time; attendees estimated 3,000. Preserve separately; do not combine or convert to bounds.
threshold_50_evidence: Each separately attributed estimate is above 50: Carabineros 500–600, the embedded police X post around 450 at one route point/time, and attendees around 3,000. Do not combine estimates or assign numeric bounds. Independent effective-admissibility review approved use of the S051 body with the original 231-input map caveat retained in G003.

title.summary: Title reflects the reported 15 January Iquique march and its reported security/crime concern; body use approved on effective-admissibility review, with the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003.

start_date.summary: Article body explicitly dates the march to 15 January 2022; effective admissibility was approved; the original 231-input map scope caveat remains recorded in G003.

end_date.summary: No verified physical end date; do not impute month-end.

location.summary: Body reports Plaza Prat and a route through main avenues toward Cavancha; effective admissibility was approved; the original 231-input map scope caveat remains recorded in G003.

scope.summary: Only Iquique location reported; no national coordination evidence.

organizer.summary: Specific organizer not established; source describes citizen-led gathering.

demands.summary: Body reports calls for authorities/government to respond to crime and insecurity; effective admissibility approved with the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003.

participants_original.summary: Separate attributions retained: Carabineros 500–600; police X around 450 at a specific route point/time; attendees around 3,000. Not pooled.

participants_min.summary: No combined numeric bound is assigned because the source attributions differ. The separately reported estimates each exceed 50; S051 use was approved on effective-admissibility review with the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Each separately reported estimate is substantially above 50, with effective admissibility approved and the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown: attempted aggression/harassment toward migrants is not evidence of protester violence against the state.

state_response.summary: All dimensions unknown except no arrests reported at publication time; preventive police intervention toward an unclear action/target is not coded as dispersal.

state_response.arrests.summary: No arrests reported at article time only.

notes: Observed first-pass body reports ask for government action on insecurity/crime; it describes the march itself as peaceful. Police intervention to prevent attempted aggression/harassment toward migrants does not establish protester violence against the state or a crowd-dispersal attempt. No-arrests statement applies only at report time. The preserved body read followed the original 231-input map, which omitted two nested physical history ledgers; independent effective-admissibility review approved use with this scope caveat retained in G003. The old map is unchanged. Keep distinct from the 30 January march and 2021 rallies.

title: Iquique march against crime and uncontrolled migration
location: Plaza Prat to Cavancha and Playa Brava, Iquique
participants_original: BioBioChile (S064) reports more than 6,000 in the 30 January main march; Cooperativa (S023) independently reports more than 4,000. Preserve source-attributed estimates separately; do not combine or derive numeric bounds. BioBioChile separately reports an approximately 500-person subgroup toward Avenida Aeropuerto/Las Rosas; do not add it to the main count.
threshold_50_evidence: S064 (>6,000) and independent S023 (>4,000) each separately exceed the 50-person threshold for the 30 January main march. Effective admissibility for S064 was approved with the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003. Keep estimates separate; no numeric participant bound is assigned.

title.summary: S064 and independently read S023 describe the 30 January Iquique march against insecurity and irregular immigration; S064 body use approved on effective-admissibility review with the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003.

start_date.summary: Both S064 and S023 date the distinct Iquique march to Sunday 30 January 2022; S064 body use approved on effective-admissibility review with the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003.

end_date.summary: No physical end date established; do not infer month-end.

location.summary: Body reports departure from Plaza Prat and route to Cavancha and Playa Brava; subgroup later moved to Avenida Aeropuerto/Las Rosas.

scope.summary: Only Iquique locations cited; national organization not established.

organizer.summary: No named organizer established in inspected source.

demands.summary: S064 says participants marched against the government over crime/homicides, seeking greater security and immigration-entry control. S023 independently describes the march against insecurity/irregular immigration; a separate next-day union leader quote should not automatically be transferred as a 30 January organizer demand.

participants_original.summary: S064 reports >6,000 and S023 independently reports >4,000 for the main march. Keep the source estimates separately attributed; neither is converted to an event-level numeric bound. S064 separately reports an approximately 500-person camp-side subgroup, which is not added.

participants_min.summary: No event-level numeric bound is coded. S064 reports >6,000 and independently read S023 reports >4,000 for the main march; retain the separate attributions, do not combine or convert them to a bound. Both separately support the 50-person threshold. S064 effective admissibility was approved with the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: S064 (>6,000) and independent S023 (>4,000) each separately exceed 50. Effective-admissibility review approved S064 use with the original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003. Keep estimates separate; no numeric bound is coded.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown for violence against the state. S023 reports a foreigner beaten while confronting the crowd and dismantling of street tents; violence against a civilian is not evidence of protester violence against state actors.

state_response.summary: S064 and S023 report no arrests/no serious disorder at their respective report times. Camp-side police route blocking is not shown as dispersal of the main march; no other response dimension is established.

state_response.arrests.summary: S064 reports no detainees at its report time; S023 separately reports no arrests/no COP deployment needed for the march. These are time-limited reports.

notes: Observed body explicitly says the march was against the government over increased crime/homicides and called for security and migration-entry control. It separately describes about 500 people approaching a migrant camp and police blocking some access routes to prevent that advance; this is not itself an attempt to disperse the main march. The article says no arrests and no serious disorder at report time; COP intervention was not needed. Some attendees wanted to destroy an abandoned installation, but actual destruction/state-directed violence is not reported. The preserved S064 body read followed the original 231-input map, which omitted two nested physical history ledgers; independent effective-admissibility review approved use with the scope caveat retained in G003. The old map is unchanged. Separate from 15 January march and 31 January stoppage; do not merge with 2021 rallies. Cooperativa S023 was subsequently opened under a fresh stable 233-input recursive gate and independently reports >4,000 for this 30 January march. Keep this estimate separate from S064 (>6,000) and do not infer a shared bound. S023 reports a foreigner beaten during confrontation; this is civilian-directed violence, not evidence of violence against the state. S064 use was independently approved on effective-admissibility review with its original 231-input map scope caveat retained in G003; S023 is a separate corroborating source, not a rewrite of that old map. Keep separate from the 15 January march, 31 January stoppage, and 2021 rallies.
open_questions: Whether the civilian beating and dismantling of tents bear on any separate violence coding; do not transfer this to violence against the state.
Physical end and response dimensions beyond time-scoped no-arrests remain unknown.

title: Arica road-access blockade over crime and insecurity
location: Southern access to Arica via Ruta 5 Norte; ADN reports continued blockades at Valle de Lluta and Acha on 1 February
participants_original: BioBioChile: a group of 1,000, then more than 1,000; Meganoticias: approximately 1,000; ADN: around 1,000 citing local media.
threshold_50_evidence: Three reports place the gathering near or above 1,000, although ADN relays local media. Each supports turnout well above 50; no artificially precise range assigned.

title.summary: Two body-read contemporary reports describe an Arica road blockade over crime/violence and insecurity.

start_date.summary: BioBioChile and Meganoticias locate the start around 19:00 Monday 31 January; ADN reports a next-morning continuation on 1 February.

end_date.summary: ADN reports blockades continued 1 February at two access areas; physical end is unknown.

location.summary: Southern access on Ruta 5 Norte; ADN reports northern Valle de Lluta and southern Acha next morning.

scope.summary: Local Arica gathering; regional/national coordination not established.

organizer.summary: Mainly transport workers/truckers; specific group/convener not named. Call circulated on social media.

demands.summary: Reports describe objection to rising crime/violence, insecurity, and irregular migration. A direct protester demand of government is not verified; target pending.

participants_original.summary: BioBioChile: “1,000 people” then “more than 1,000”; Meganoticias “near 1,000”; ADN “around 1,000,” explicitly citing local media.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Separate contemporary sources report a gathering near or above 1,000; threshold clear.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown; road blockade is reported, but violence against the state is not described.

state_response.summary: Unknown; announced ministerial travel and a future conversation with gremios are not a completed meeting/accommodation, and no other response is reported.

notes: Freshly gated body reports identify a 31 January action beginning around 19:00, mainly by truckers, using a social-media call. The public-safety/migration issue is clear but whether protesters directly demanded government action remains unresolved. A minister announced a future trip/dialogue; no completed meeting with these protesters is reported, so accommodation remains unknown. ADN reports blockades continued on 1 February; exact physical end is unknown. Protester violence against the state and police response are not established. Do not merge with Iquique gatherings.

title: Tarapacá stoppage and related public actions over crime, insecurity and migration
location: Iquique and access routes, with a related action reported at the Alto Hospicio municipality; multiple activity sites are not individually resolved.
organizer: Trade, transport, port and hotel guilds with citizen participation; a complete coalition roster is not identified.
participants_original: No observed participant count is reported for the 31 January stoppage, blockades or merchant march. Cooperativa records an expectation of at least 300 taxi drivers and a plan for about 40 collective-taxi vehicles; neither is an actual participant count. Airport passengers and public officials are not turnout.
threshold_50_evidence: Several blockades, a merchant procession and taxi-caravan activity are described, but none has a verified count of assembled participants. The reported 300 taxi drivers were expected and the 40 vehicles were planned; neither proves a crowd of 50. Retain pending_threshold.

title.summary: Both opened sources report the 31 January Tarapacá/Iquique regional stoppage over security/crime and migration concerns.

start_date.summary: S043 dates the Monday action to 31 January and attributes first blockades to around 02:00; S023 live entries describe 31 January actions. The page publication date is not used as the onset.

end_date.summary: No specific physical end is established for all gatherings/blockades; keep null rather than use restoration-of-traffic remarks or page update time.

location.summary: Reports include Iquique route/access blockades and merchants marching toward the regional presidential delegation; a separate Alto Hospicio municipality action is also described. Do not infer one continuous assembly across all sites.

scope.summary: The call and activity are described as regional in Tarapacá, with Iquique and Alto Hospicio examples; national coordination is not established.

organizer.summary: S043 names trade, transport, port and hotel guilds; S023 names additional merchant and taxi groups. A complete formal coalition is not identified.

demands.summary: Reported grievances concern crime, insecurity and migration. A port-guild leader says actions of this type are needed to draw government attention; this is a government-facing political-process demand. Do not transfer the mayor’s separate policy statements to protesters.

participants_original.summary: Neither article reports an observed count for 31 January assemblies. The 300 taxi drivers figure is expected, not counted; 40 vehicles is a plan.

participants_min.summary: No conservative numerical floor is established for any identified 31 January gathering; do not use transport impacts, prior-day turnout, expected drivers, or planned vehicles.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Gathering threshold remains unresolved; no observed attendance count. Keep pending_threshold.

protester_violence.summary: Unknown. S023 says tomatoes were thrown at the front of the Alto Hospicio municipality but does not establish target, injury, damage or relation to another site’s gathering.

state_response.summary: Only a time-scoped no-arrests/no-serious-incident statement and police dialogue to restore traffic are reported. No event-linked accommodation, violence by state, or dispersal effort is established; an announced future ministerial visit is not a completed meeting.

state_response.accommodation.summary: A ministerial visit and meeting were announced for the next day; no completed meeting/agreement or addressed demand is reported.

state_response.arrests.summary: The presidential delegate said at 15:48 on 31 January that no one had been arrested by then; this is report-time only.

state_response.beatings.summary: No state beating of protesters is reported.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Carabineros dialogue and traffic-flow work are described, but not a warning, push, tear gas or other action aimed at dispersing an assembled protest crowd.

state_response.ignore.summary: No specific deliberate state ignoring of the protest is established.

notes: Provisional 31 January candidate only. It includes a regional stoppage and several reported public actions, but exact gathering units across roadblocks, merchant procession, taxi caravan and Alto Hospicio are not resolved and no observed crowd count establishes the 50-person threshold. Keep pending_threshold; do not turn the reported 300 expected taxi drivers, 40 planned vehicles, hundreds of affected passengers, or >4,000/>6,000 previous-day marchers into turnout. The port-guild leader’s attention-to-government quote supports a state-directed political-process target; officials’ own statements are not protester demands. The reported tomato throwing needs target/impact clarification. Keep separate from 15 January and 30 January Iquique marches and 31 January Arica blockade; the 2021 Iquique protest is only historical context. A 200-person Laguna Verde march appears in a 1 February 12:19 update and is not assigned to January without a verified date/episode link.
open_questions: Obtain a source with an observed crowd count for each specific 31 January gathering; no threshold from anticipated taxi drivers or planned vehicles.
Resolve whether the multi-site actions are one regional episode or separate gatherings; preserve locations and phases until resolved.
Clarify the tomato-throwing target/impact and whether it belongs to a codeable public event.
Verify physical ends and any completed state response; announced next-day ministerial plans are not accommodation.
Determine exact date and episode relation for the 200-person Laguna Verde report in the 1 February live-report update.

title: Temuco protest against Juan Sutil-backed reservoir project
location: Outside the Superintendencia del Medio Ambiente, then at the Regional Delegation of La Araucanía, Temuco
participants_original: BioBioChile reports communities from Nueva Imperial, Cholchol, Galvarino and Temuco protesting, but gives no participant count or estimate. The number assembled is unknown; do not infer a crowd size from the plural “communities” or the article description.
threshold_50_evidence: No attendance count or estimate is reported. Whether at least 50 people assembled is unresolved; keep pending evidence.

title.summary: The article reports a protest against the Juan Sutil-backed reservoir project; the candidate title does not infer a formal organizer or a direct state demand.

start_date.summary: The article is dated 28 January 2022 at 13:53 and describes the protest as occurring that day. This supports day-level occurrence, not an exact start time.

end_date.summary: No physical end date or end time is reported.

location.summary: The article says the protest was outside the Superintendencia del Medio Ambiente and moved to the Regional Delegation of La Araucanía, in Temuco.

scope.summary: The gathering is reported in Temuco; no broader coordination is established.

organizer.summary: No named organizer or formal organizing body established.

demands.summary: The article reports allegations about environmental rules, Indigenous consultation, river alteration and wetlands. It does not establish a clear demand directed to a Chilean state actor; target remains unresolved.

participants_original.summary: No attendance figure is reported. The named source communities do not establish number assembled.

participants_min.summary: No conservative numeric lower bound is available; numeric bounds remain null.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The article supplies no crowd count or estimate, so the 50-person threshold is unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: No protester violence against the state is reported.

state_response.summary: The article reports no police action, dispersal, arrests, accommodation, or other state response.

state_response.arrests.summary: No arrest information is reported; retain unknown rather than infer no arrests.

notes: Provisional candidate from the S063 full article read in window2. The article is dated 28 January and describes a protest that day, but exact onset and physical end are unknown. It reports the route and grievances without an attendance count or a clear demand to a state actor; both the 50-person threshold and state-directed target remain unresolved. Do not infer a state target solely from the public venues or transfer allegations into a coded demand. S060/S067/S070 may overlap but remain unverified; do not merge without episode-level evidence. S063 source-card metadata was reconciled after window2 closed; the full body is not stored.
open_questions: Find an observed attendance count or estimate for the 28 January Temuco gathering and resolve whether at least 50 assembled.
Determine whether participants made a demand directed to a Chilean state actor or were protesting a private project without a state-directed target.
Verify exact start and physical end, any police/state response, and whether S060/S067/S070 report the same gathering.
